### CVE-2026-8863 — CVE-2026-8863
- Assigner: certcc | Published: 2026-06-09 | Updated: 2026-06-10 | Max CVSS: 7.8
- CWE: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature; CWE-354: Improper Validation of Integrity Check Value
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 7.8 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Multiple Microsoft-sigend UEFI SHIM bootloaders are vulnerable to SecureBoot bypass. An attacker with administrative privileges or the ability to modify the boot process could use one of the vulnerable shim bootloaders to bypass Secure Boot protections and execute arbitrary code before the operating system loads. Specific UEFI DBX update is required to block these vulnerable boot loaders.

### CVE-2026-10037 — Sandbox Escape in Ubuntu OpenJDK Packages via xdg-desktop-portal
- Assigner: canonical | Published: 2026-07-08 | Updated: 2026-07-14 | Max CVSS: 8.8
- CWE: CWE-20 CWE-20 Improper input validation
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 8.8 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

A sandbox escape vulnerability exists in the OpenJDK packages provided in Ubuntu. The .jar MIME handlers installed by these packages execute files marked as executable when the mailcap package is installed. A compromised or malicious sandboxed application with access to the OpenURI portal via xdg-desktop-portal-gtk can write a malicious .jar file to the host file system, set its executable bit, and trigger the handler to execute arbitrary code outside of the sandbox environment.

### CVE-2026-15560 — Openjdk-orb: unauthed class loading via iiop in eap
- Assigner: redhat | Published: 2026-08-11 | Updated: 2026-11-22 | Max CVSS: 8.1
- CWE: CWE-829 Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 8.1 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total
- CVSS 3.1 (nvd:secalert@redhat.com:Secondary): 8.1 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`

when EAP runs with -secmgr, the openjdk-orb's JDKBridge honours attacker-supplied CDR codebase URLs during object unmarshalling on :3528, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to load and instantiate arbitrary classes from a remote URL in the server JVM before EJB security interceptors run.

**workarounds:** Mitigation for this issue is either not available or the currently available options do not meet the Red Hat Product Security criteria comprising ease of use and deployment, applicability to widespread installation base, or stability. Users of affected JBoss EAP streams should apply the openjdk-orb updates provided for their supported EAP version through the usual update channels.

### CVE-2026-15564 — Wildfly-ejb: wildfly-iiop-openjdk: eap iiop listeners may permit unauthed deserialization
- Assigner: redhat | Published: 2026-10-29 | Updated: 2026-11-22 | Max CVSS: 7.4
- CWE: CWE-829 Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.4 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total
- CVSS 3.1 (nvd:secalert@redhat.com:Secondary): 7.4 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`

Wildfly's IIOP listener may permit deserialization of input streams before authentication is performed. An attacker who can gain access to the IIOP port may be able to construct and send malicious objects and achieve deserialization, if the target EJB allows untyped method parameters, and depending on the potential gadget chains available in the running classpath.

**workarounds:** Restrict network reachability to the IIOP listener (default TCP port 3528) so that only localhost or authorized management networks can access it.

1. Restrict port exposure using firewalld:
```bash
firewall-cmd --permanent --remove-port=3528/tcp
firewall-cmd --reload
```

2. If CORBA/IIOP interoperability is not required by deployed applications, remove the IIOP subsystem using the JBoss Management CLI:
```bash
jboss-cli.sh --connect --command="/subsystem=iiop-openjdk:remove"
```

Caveats:
Removing the IIOP subsystem will break remote EJB invocations or external services that rely on CORBA/IIOP protocols.

Warning:
Applying firewall changes or removing server subsystems will disrupt active client connections and requires reloading the server configuration or restarting the JBoss EAP service to take full effect.

### CVE-2026-19611 — Wildfly-elytron: org.wildfly.security/wildfly-elytron-password-impl: wildfly-elytron: password keyspace reduction via nfkc fullwidth folding
- Assigner: redhat | Published: 2026-08-20 | Updated: 2026-11-22 | Max CVSS: 7.4
- CWE: CWE-173 Improper Handling of Alternate Encoding
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.4 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total
- CVSS 3.1 (nvd:secalert@redhat.com:Secondary): 7.4 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N`

A flaw was found in WildFly Elytron. Password hashing and verification normalize input with Unicode NFKC, which can collapse fullwidth characters to ASCII equivalents. A remote attacker can more easily guess affected passwords by using an ASCII-only dictionary against accounts whose passwords were intended to include those non-ASCII characters, leading to unauthorized access.

**workarounds:** Mitigation for this issue is either not available or the currently available options do not meet the Red Hat Product Security criteria comprising ease of use and deployment, applicability to widespread installation base, or stability.

Vulnerability in the Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition product of Oracle Java SE (component: AWT, JavaFX). This vulnerability does not apply to Java deployments, typically in servers, that load and run only trusted code (e.g., code installed by an administrator). - CWE: Easily exploitable vulnerability allows unauthenticated attacker with network access via HTTP to compromise Oracle HTTP Server, Oracle Weblogic Server Proxy Plug-in.  While the vulnerability is in Oracle HTTP Server, Oracle Weblogic Server Proxy Plug-in, attacks may significantly impact additional products (scope change).  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in  unauthorized creation, deletion or modification access to critical data or all Oracle HTTP Server, Oracle Weblogic Server Proxy Plug-in accessible data as well as  unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle HTTP Server, Oracle Weblogic Server Proxy Plug-in accessible data.; CWE-284 CWE-284 Improper Access Control
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 10 CRITICAL `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=active, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total
- **CISA KEV**: added 2026-08-24, ransomware=Unknown — Oracle HTTP Server and Oracle Weblogic Server Proxy Plug-in Improper Access Control Vulnerability

Vulnerability in the Oracle HTTP Server, Oracle Weblogic Server Proxy Plug-in product of Oracle Fusion Middleware (component: Weblogic Server Proxy Plug-in for Apache HTTP Server, Weblogic Server Proxy Plug-in for IIS).  Supported versions that are affected are 12.2.1.4.0, 14.1.1.0.0 and  14.1.2.0.0. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows unauthenticated attacker with network access via HTTP to compromise Oracle HTTP Server, Oracle Weblogic Server Proxy Plug-in.  While the vulnerability is in Oracle HTTP Server, Oracle Weblogic Server Proxy Plug-in, attacks may significantly impact additional products (scope change).  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in  unauthorized creation, deletion or modification access to critical data or all Oracle HTTP Server, Oracle Weblogic Server Proxy Plug-in accessible data as well as  unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle HTTP Server, Oracle Weblogic Server Proxy Plug-in accessible data. Note: Affected version for Weblogic Server Proxy Plug-in for IIS is 12.2.1.4.0 only. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 10.0 (Confidentiality and Integrity impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N).

Affected:
- Oracle Corporation / Oracle HTTP Server, Oracle Weblogic Server Proxy Plug-in: affected 12.2.1.4.0 (semver); affected 14.1.1.0.0 (semver); affected 14.1.2.0.0 (semver)

### CVE-2026-22184 — zlib <= 1.3.1.2 untgz Global Buffer Overflow in TGZfname()
- Assigner: VulnCheck | Published: 2026-01-07 | Updated: 2026-09-01 | Max CVSS: 8.6
- CWE: CWE-787 CWE-787 Out-of-bounds Write; CWE-120 Buffer Copy without Checking Size of Input ('Classic Buffer Overflow')
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 4.6 MEDIUM `CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:A/VC:L/VI:N/VA:L/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total
- CVSS 3.1 (redhat-SADP): 8.6 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:H`

zlib versions up to and including 1.3.1.2 include a global buffer overflow in the untgz utility located under contrib/untgz. The vulnerability is limited to the standalone demonstration utility and does not affect the core zlib compression library. The flaw occurs when a user executes the untgz command with an excessively long archive name supplied via the command line, leading to an out-of-bounds write in a fixed-size global buffer.

### CVE-2026-25646 — LIBPNG has a heap buffer overflow in png_set_quantize
- Assigner: GitHub_M | Published: 2026-02-10 | Updated: 2026-09-01 | Max CVSS: 8.3
- CWE: CWE-122 CWE-122: Heap-based Buffer Overflow; CWE-126 CWE-126: Buffer Over-read; CWE-125 Out-of-bounds Read
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 8.3 HIGH `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:L/VI:L/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=partial
- CVSS 3.1 (redhat-SADP): 7 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:H`

LIBPNG is a reference library for use in applications that read, create, and manipulate PNG (Portable Network Graphics) raster image files. Prior to 1.6.55, an out-of-bounds read vulnerability exists in the png_set_quantize() API function. When the function is called with no histogram and the number of colors in the palette is more than twice the maximum supported by the user's display, certain palettes will cause the function to enter into an infinite loop that reads past the end of an internal heap-allocated buffer. The images that trigger this vulnerability are valid per the PNG specification. This vulnerability is fixed in 1.6.55.

Affected:
- pnggroup / libpng: affected < 1.6.55
- Red Hat / Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10: unaffected 2:1.6.40-8.el10_1.2 <* (rpm)

- CVSS 3.1 (redhat-SADP): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`

Vulnerability in the Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition product of Oracle Java SE (component: Networking).  Supported versions that are affected are Oracle Java SE: 8u481-perf, 11.0.30, 17.0.18, 21.0.10, 25.0.2, 26; Oracle GraalVM for JDK: 17.0.18 and  21.0.10; Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition: 21.3.17. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows unauthenticated attacker with network access via multiple protocols to compromise Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition. Note: This vulnerability can be exploited by using APIs in the specified Component, e.g., through a web service which supplies data to the APIs. This vulnerability also applies to Java deployments, typically in clients running sandboxed Java Web Start applications or sandboxed Java applets, that load and run untrusted code (e.g., code that comes from the internet) and rely on the Java sandbox for security. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 7.5 (Availability impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H).

### CVE-2026-54513 — jackson-databind: Array subtype allowlist bypass in BasicPolymorphicTypeValidator (allowIfSubTypeIsArray)
- Assigner: GitHub_M | Published: 2026-06-23 | Updated: 2026-09-14 | Max CVSS: 8.1
- CWE: CWE-184 CWE-184: Incomplete List of Disallowed Inputs; CWE-184 Incomplete List of Disallowed Inputs
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 8.1 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total
- CVSS 3.1 (redhat-SADP): 8.1 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`

jackson-databind contains the general-purpose data-binding functionality and tree-model for Jackson Data Processor. From 2.10.0 until 2.18.8, 2.21.4, and 3.1.4, BasicPolymorphicTypeValidator.Builder.allowIfSubTypeIsArray() allowlists any array type based only on clazz.isArray(), without validating the array's component (element) type against the configured allowlist. A PTV built with allowIfSubTypeIsArray() plus an explicit concrete-type allowlist therefore still permits EvilType[] even though EvilType is not allowlisted. When Jackson deserializes the elements and no per-element type IDs are present, it instantiates the component type directly with no further PTV check, bypassing the allowlist. This vulnerability is fixed in 2.18.8, 2.21.4, and 3.1.4.

- FasterXML / jackson-databind: affected >= 2.10.0, < 2.18.8; affected >= 2.19.0, < 2.21.4; affected >= 3.0.0, < 3.1.4

### CVE-2026-57898
- Assigner: eclipse | Published: 2026-07-14 | Updated: 2026-08-31 | Max CVSS: 9
- CWE: CWE-22 CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal'); CWE-73 CWE-73: External Control of File Name or Path
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 9 CRITICAL `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

In Eclipse BaSyx Java Server SDK versions 2.0.0-milestone-05 to 2.0.0-milestone-12, deployments using the MongoDB backend are vulnerable to an unauthenticated arbitrary file write through the AAS thumbnail API.




The AAS thumbnail upload path accepted a client-controlled fileName request parameter and passed it through repository file handling as both a repository key and, during thumbnail retrieval, a local filesystem path. With the MongoDB file repository, the supplied filename was treated as an opaque GridFS key and was not normalized or restricted as a filesystem path. A remote attacker could upload thumbnail content using an absolute or traversal-style filename, then trigger thumbnail retrieval so that the uploaded bytes were written to the attacker-chosen path on the server filesystem.




This could allow writing files anywhere the Java process has permission to write and may lead to remote code execution. The default InMemory backend is not affected by this specific path because it normalizes and restricts file paths to its temporary directory.




The issue is fixed in Eclipse BaSyx Java Server SDK 2.0.0-milestone-13.

Affected:
- Eclipse Foundation / Eclipse BaSyx - Java Server SDK: affected 2.0.0-milestone-05 <2.0.0-milestone-13 (semver)

Credits: Eclipse Foundation Security Team

References:
- https://gitlab.eclipse.org/security/cve-assignment/-/work_items/159

CVSS 3.1 Base Score 7.6 (Confidentiality, Integrity and Availability impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:H/A:L).

### CVE-2026-81624 — Undertow-core: undertow: websocketcontainer defaults for buffers and timeouts are infinite
- Assigner: redhat | Published: 2026-08-31 | Updated: 2026-11-04 | Max CVSS: 7.5
- CWE: CWE-770 Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

Undertow is a flexible performant web server used in JBoss EAP and WildFly. A flaw was found in how Undertow handles WebSocket connections. Specifically, certain configuration limits like message buffer sizes and session timeouts cannot be adjusted and default to being unlimited. This allows a remote attacker to send large amounts of data or maintain connections indefinitely, potentially crashing the server by exhausting its memory or other resources.

**workarounds:** Mitigation for this issue is either not available or the currently available options do not meet the Red Hat Product Security criteria comprising ease of use and deployment, applicability to widespread installation base, or stability.

Affected:
- Red Hat / Red Hat build of Apache Camel for Spring Boot 4: 
- Red Hat / Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10: 
- Red Hat / Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8: 
- Red Hat / Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8: 
- Red Hat / Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9: 
- Red Hat / Red Hat Fuse 7: 
- Red Hat / Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform 7:

### CVE-2026-84725 — Openjdk-orb: incomplete fix for cve-2026-15560,unauthed class loading via iiop in eap
- Assigner: redhat | Published: 2026-10-28 | Updated: 2026-11-22 | Max CVSS: 8.1
- CWE: CWE-829 Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 8.1 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total
- CVSS 3.1 (nvd:secalert@redhat.com:Secondary): 8.1 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`

when EAP runs with -secmgr, the openjdk-orb's JDKBridge honours attacker-supplied CDR codebase URLs during object unmarshalling on :3528, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to load and instantiate arbitrary classes from a remote URL in the server JVM before EJB security interceptors run.

**workarounds:** To mitigate this flaw, restrict access to the IIOP service (TCP port 3528) to trusted networks using firewall rules, or disable the IIOP subsystem if CORBA is not required by deployed applications.

To restrict or remove external access to port 3528 using firewalld:
```
firewall-cmd --permanent --remove-port=3528/tcp
firewall-cmd --reload
```

Warning: Reloading the firewall configuration may briefly interrupt network traffic. If removing the iiop-openjdk subsystem from the JBoss EAP configuration (standalone.xml or domain.xml), a full server restart is required, causing temporary service downtime.

Caveats: Blocking port 3528 or disabling the IIOP subsystem will prevent legitimate remote clients from communicating over IIOP/CORBA

Affected:

### CVE-2026-84823 — Org.wildfly.core: wildfly: path traversal in take-snapshot discloses the server configuration to the monitor role
- Assigner: redhat | Published: 2026-10-15 | Updated: 2026-11-06 | Max CVSS: 7.1
- CWE: CWE-22 Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.1 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:L/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=partial

A flaw was found in WildFly. A user with the `Monitor` role, which is the lowest standard Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) role, can exploit a path traversal vulnerability in the `take-snapshot` operation. By manipulating the `name` parameter, this user can write a copy of the server configuration to an arbitrary location. This allows the `Monitor` role to read back the server configuration, including sensitive credentials, which would otherwise be restricted by RBAC, leading to information disclosure.

**workarounds:** To mitigate this issue, restrict access to the WildFly management interface to trusted networks and users. Implement firewall rules to limit network reachability to the management ports. Additionally, review existing Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) assignments within WildFly and ensure that users are granted only the minimum necessary privileges, adhering to the principle of least privilege. Reviewing role assignments might impact functionality if users genuinely require the `Monitor` role for their operations.

### CVE-2026-85634 — Wildfly-core: wildfly-core: deployer rbac role privilege escalation via path traversal in deployment name
- Assigner: redhat | Published: 2026-10-15 | Updated: 2026-11-22 | Max CVSS: 8.8
- CWE: CWE-22 Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 8.8 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total
- CVSS 3.1 (nvd:secalert@redhat.com:Secondary): 8.8 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`

A flaw was found in the ContentRepositoryImpl.copyExplodedContent function of the wildfly-core library, which is used by WildFly and JBoss EAP to manage server deployments. The issue occurs when the library processes an unsanitized deployment name. Due to a missing containment check, an attacker with the Deployer RBAC role can use path traversal sequences to access files outside the restricted deployment directory. This can allow the attacker to delete arbitrary directories or create files with arbitrary content, leading to a full privilege escalation to the management SuperUser role.

**workarounds:** Mitigation for this issue is either not available or the currently available options do not meet the Red Hat Product Security criteria comprising ease of use and deployment, applicability to widespread installation base, or stability.

### CVE-2026-89058 — Resteasy-core: resteasy: corsfilter reflects arbitrary origin with credentials under wildcard config
- Assigner: redhat | Published: 2026-09-18 | Updated: 2026-11-22 | Max CVSS: 7.4
- CWE: CWE-346 Origin Validation Error; CWE-942 CWE-942 Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.4 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=partial
- CVSS 3.1 (nvd:secalert@redhat.com:Secondary): 7.4 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:N`

A flaw was found in RESTEasy's CorsFilter, which, when configured to allow all origins ("*"), reflects the request's Origin header back in the Access-Control-Allow-Origin response together with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. This permissive cross-origin policy allows a malicious website to make credentialed cross-origin requests and read authenticated responses from a victim's session, resulting in a loss of confidentiality.

Affected:
- Red Hat / RESTEasy: affected 0 <6.2.19.Final (maven); affected 7.0.0.Alpha1 <7.0.5.Final (maven)
- Red Hat / Red Hat Build of Apache Camel 3.33.4.redhat: unaffected 6.2.19.Final-redhat-00003 <* (rpm)

### CVE-2026-89059 — Resteasy-core: resteasy: iioimageprovider unbounded image decode (decompression-bomb dos)
- Assigner: redhat | Published: 2026-09-18 | Updated: 2026-11-22 | Max CVSS: 7.5
- CWE: CWE-409 Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification)
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial
- CVSS 3.1 (nvd:secalert@redhat.com:Secondary): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`

A flaw was found in RESTEasy's IIOImageProvider, which decodes attacker-supplied image request bodies without enforcing any limit on the declared image dimensions or pixel count. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can send a small crafted image declaring enormous dimensions to trigger a very large memory allocation, exhausting the JVM heap and resulting in a denial of service.

Affected:
- Red Hat / RESTEasy: affected 0 <6.2.19.Final (maven); affected 7.0.0.Alpha1 <7.0.5.Final (maven)
- Red Hat / Red Hat Build of Apache Camel 3.33.4.redhat: unaffected 6.2.19.Final-redhat-00003 <* (rpm)

- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 8.7 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N`

Supported versions that are affected are 12.2.1.4.0 and  14.1.2.1.0. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows high privileged attacker with network access via SOAP to compromise Oracle Identity Manager Connector. ### CVE-2026-93494 — Io.netty/netty-codec-stomp: netty: bytebuf leak in stompsubframedecoder when a frame body is never terminated
- Assigner: redhat | Published: 2026-09-18 | Updated: 2026-09-25 | Max CVSS: 7.5
- CWE: CWE-1035 CWE-1035
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

A flaw was found in Netty's StompSubframeDecoder component. A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability by sending a specially crafted STOMP frame body without its terminating null byte. This causes the decoder to allocate a ByteBuf (a buffer for bytes) that is never released, leading to a permanent memory leak. Over time, this uncontrolled memory consumption can result in a Denial of Service (DoS) for the application using the affected STOMP codec.

**workarounds:** See https://github.com/netty/netty/security/advisories/GHSA-ghg5-c4jg-8q5j for fixed versions and remediation guidance.

### CVE-2026-93576 — Io.netty/netty-codec-smtp: netty netty-codec-smtp — smtp command-name field is not crlf-validated (incomplete fix of cve-2025-59419)
- Assigner: redhat | Published: 2026-09-18 | Updated: 2026-09-25 | Max CVSS: 7.5
- CWE: CWE-93 Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences ('CRLF Injection')
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

A flaw was found in Netty netty-codec-smtp. The component does not properly validate Carriage Return (CR) and Line Feed (LF) characters in the SMTP command-name field. A remote attacker, if an application routes untrusted input into this field, can embed CR/LF characters to inject arbitrary SMTP commands. This can lead to SMTP command smuggling, allowing for unauthorized email relay or spoofing of sender/recipient addresses. While the impact is significant, the real-world exploitability is considered lower as applications typically do not place user-controlled data in the command-name field.

**workarounds:** See https://github.com/netty/netty/security/advisories/GHSA-5vh9-c45f-rf7p for fixed versions and remediation guidance.

### CVE-2026-93998 — Keycloak-core: keycloak-core: saml adapter does not bind signed assertions to the configured identity provider issuer
- Assigner: redhat | Published: 2026-11-05 | Updated: 2026-11-06 | Max CVSS: 7.4
- CWE: CWE-347 Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.4 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

A flaw was found in the SAML adapter component of Keycloak, which is used to secure applications with SAML-based authentication. The adapter fails to verify that the issuer of a signed SAML assertion matches the expected identity provider configured for the application. If multiple identity providers share the same trusted signing key, an attacker who controls one of those providers can create a validly signed assertion to log into the application as any user, potentially gaining full administrative control.

**workarounds:** Mitigation for this issue is either not available or the currently available options do not meet the Red Hat Product Security criteria comprising ease of use and deployment, applicability to widespread installation base, or stability.

--- CME Mitigation Guidance (2026-11-06) ---
Disclaimer: The following mitigation solutions are provided as a courtesy, pending the application of an official patch. This content was generated utilizing AI tools in conjunction with data from https://cmetaxonomy.org. Customers are advised to independently evaluate and test these temporary mitigations within their own infrastructure.

The highest-value action is to enforce strict verification of the SAML assertion Issuer attribute against the configured identity provider entity ID in the Keycloak SAML adapter: upgrade to Red Hat build of Keycloak 26.4.17, 26.6.8 (or the corresponding fixed Red Hat builds), which verify that the Issuer attribute in the received SAML response and assertion strictly matches the configured identity provider entity ID, closing all 2 injection vectors (cross-tenant SAML assertion injection, shared-key sibling issuer assertion forging). Until patched, this is a concern on Applications secured using the Keycloak SAML adapter where signing keys are shared across multiple identity providers or tenants, so Ensure signing keys are strictly isolated per identity provider and never shared across multiple issuers or tenants. These controls limit blast radius and contain exploitation, but they do not fix the underlying missing SAML issuer validation defect — apply the upstream patch to fully remediate.

Highest-impact CME: CME-1315 Allowlist-Preferred Input Validation (Deny-by-Default Filtering) (high)

### CVE-2026-96453 — Org.keycloak/keycloak-admin-cli: keycloak-admin-cli: kcadm custom truststore accepts arbitrary self-signed certificates
- Assigner: redhat | Published: 2026-11-05 | Updated: 2026-11-09 | Max CVSS: 8
- CWE: CWE-295 Improper Certificate Validation
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 8 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

A flaw was found in the Keycloak Admin CLI kcadm tool, which is used by administrators to manage Keycloak servers from the command line. When a custom truststore is provided to verify the server identity, the tool incorrectly accepts any self-signed certificate as long as the hostname matches. This allows a network attacker to impersonate the Keycloak server, steal administrative credentials, and perform unauthorized management actions.

**workarounds:** Mitigation for this issue is either not available or the currently available options do not meet the Red Hat Product Security criteria comprising ease of use and deployment, applicability to widespread installation base, or stability.

--- CME Mitigation Guidance (2026-11-06) ---
Disclaimer: The following mitigation solutions are provided as a courtesy, pending the application of an official patch. This content was generated utilizing AI tools in conjunction with data from https://cmetaxonomy.org. Customers are advised to independently evaluate and test these temporary mitigations within their own infrastructure.

The highest-value action is to disable TrustSelfSignedStrategy in the Keycloak Admin CLI HTTP client configuration and enforce validation strictly against the configured custom truststore: upgrade to Red Hat build of Keycloak 26.4.17 / 26.6.8 (or the corresponding fixed Red Hat builds), which disable TrustSelfSignedStrategy in the HTTP client and enforce certificate verification against the provided truststore, closing all 2 injection vectors (Man-in-the-Middle network interception, DNS redirection). Until patched, this is a concern on Administrators executing kcadm with a custom truststore option, so Avoid executing kcadm with custom truststores across untrusted networks, and restrict network paths and DNS resolution between client hosts and Keycloak endpoints. As a compensating measure, Cryptographically verify DNS response authenticity using DNSSEC validation to prevent DNS redirection to unauthorized servers and Isolate administrative traffic between kcadm clients and Keycloak servers into dedicated VLANs or subnets to prevent network interception. These controls limit blast radius and contain exploitation, but they do not fix the underlying certificate validation defect — apply the upstream patch to fully remediate.

Highest-impact CME: CME-203 Network Segmentation (VLANs/Subnets) (medium)

### CVE-2026-114488 — Wildfly: wildfly-iiop: wildfly-ejb3: wildfly: authentication bypass on iiop ejb invocations as csiv2 ittprincipalname accepted without transport binding
- Assigner: redhat | Published: 2026-10-29 | Updated: 2026-11-22 | Max CVSS: 7.4
- CWE: CWE-829 Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.4 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total
- CVSS 3.1 (nvd:secalert@redhat.com:Secondary): 7.4 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N`

A flaw was found in Wildfly. A remote attacker can bypass authentication on IIOP EJB invocations as the CSIv2 security interceptor accepts ITTPrincipalName identity assertions in the service context without verifying transport-level authentication, allowing a pre-auth attacker on the port 3528 to impersonate any principal on every IIOP-exposed @Remote EJB.

**workarounds:** To mitigate this vulnerability without modifying binaries, apply one or more of the following operational and configuration controls:

1. Maintain or revert caller propagation to the default 'none' setting in the IIOP subsystem configuration:
Run the following management CLI command:
`/subsystem=iiop-openjdk:write-attribute(name=caller-propagation,value=none)`
Ensure that application deployment descriptors (such as jboss-ejb3.xml) do not explicitly override caller propagation to 'supported'.

2. Restrict network reachability:
Block external access to the CORBA/IIOP port (default TCP port 3528) using firewall rules, or restrict access strictly to trusted application networks:
`firewall-cmd --remove-port=3528/tcp --permanent && firewall-cmd --reload`

3. Enforce transport-level security:
If caller propagation is required for your architecture, configure the IIOP subsystem to require SSL/TLS with client certificate authentication by setting `server-requires-ssl="true"`, or enforce mandatory authentication via the `as-context` configuration.

Caveats:
Disabling caller propagation prevents client security identity forwarding across remote IIOP EJB calls, which may impact applications relying on distributed identity propagation. Restricting firewall access will prevent external clients outside authorized networks from connecting to IIOP services.

Warning:
Applying configuration changes via the JBoss management CLI requires reloading the runtime service (`:reload`), which will temporarily interrupt active client connections.

Affected:
- Red Hat / Red Hat Fuse 7: 
- Red Hat / Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform 7: 
- Red Hat / Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform 7: 
- Red Hat / Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform 8: 
- Red Hat / Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform Expansion Pack: 
- Red Hat / Red Hat Single Sign-On 7:

- https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/CVE-2026-114488 [vdb-entry,x_refsource_REDHAT]
- https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2491619 [issue-tracking,x_refsource_REDHAT]

Vulnerability in the Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition product of Oracle Java SE (component: JSSE).  Supported versions that are affected are Oracle Java SE: 8u511-b32, 8u511-perf-b32, 11.0.33.0.2, 17.0.21.0.2, 21.0.13.0.2, 25.0.5.0.2, 27.0.1.0.2; Oracle GraalVM for JDK: 17.0.21.0.2 and  21.0.13.0.2; Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition: 21.3.20.0.2. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows unauthenticated attacker with network access via multiple protocols to compromise Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition. Note: This vulnerability can be exploited by using APIs in the specified Component, e.g., through a web service which supplies data to the APIs. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 9.1 (Confidentiality and Integrity impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N).

- Assigner: oracle | Published: 2026-11-17 | Updated: 2026-11-19 | Max CVSS: 7.1
- CWE: Easily exploitable vulnerability allows low privileged attacker with network access via multiple protocols to compromise MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster.  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in unauthorized ability to cause a hang or frequently repeatable crash (complete DOS) of MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster and  unauthorized read access to a subset of MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster accessible data.; CWE-400 CWE-400 Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.1 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=partial

Vulnerability in the MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster product of Oracle MySQL (component: Server: GIS).  Supported versions that are affected are MySQL Server: 8.4.0-8.4.13, 9.7.0-9.7.4, 26.10; MySQL Cluster: 8.0.0-8.0.50, 8.4.0-8.4.13, 9.7.0-9.7.4 and  26.10. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows low privileged attacker with network access via multiple protocols to compromise MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster.  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in unauthorized ability to cause a hang or frequently repeatable crash (complete DOS) of MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster and  unauthorized read access to a subset of MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster accessible data. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 7.1 (Confidentiality and Availability impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:H).

- Oracle Corporation / MySQL Cluster: affected 8.0.0-8.0.50; affected 8.4.0-8.4.13; affected 9.7.0-9.7.4; affected 26.10
